assumptions.choice: Added stop_method param ('percent'|'atr'|'max', default 'max') selecting the stop-loss formula; default reproduces the literal max(...)/min(...) formula from the spec while the parameter lets the caller isolate either the percent or ATR stop alone.
assumptions.reason: Spec states the stop as max(...)/min(...) but also explicitly says 'choose one method via a parameter'; the default satisfies the literal formula and the parameter satisfies the method-choice instruction.
Spec requires the reversal behavior be parameter-gated but states no default; False preserves the canonical no-pyramiding/no-re-entry default unless explicitly enabled.

assumptions.choice: Reversal (close then immediately re-enter opposite side) triggers only on the opposite-signal exit condition, not on stop-loss exits.
assumptions.reason: Spec's reversal clause reads 'reverse on opposite signals', explicitly tied to the opposite-signal exit case rather than the stop-loss case.

assumptions.choice: Stop-loss is evaluated each bar by comparing Close to the computed stop level and, if triggered, executed via a plain market self.close() rather than a resting bt.Order.Stop order.
assumptions.reason: Spec does not specify an order type/execution mechanism for the stop; canonical default directs plain buy()/sell()/close() without size, applied consistently with the next()-driven signal checks.

assumptions.choice: Use backtrader's built-in ATR(data, period=14) (Wilder-style smoothing).
assumptions.reason: Spec names 'ATR(14)' without specifying a smoothing method; backtrader's default ATR is the standard implementation.

assumptions.choice: Momentum implemented via bt.indicators.RateOfChange100(close, period=10), which computes exactly (Close[0]/Close[-10]-1)*100.
assumptions.reason: Using the built-in indicator instead of manual close[-10] indexing lets backtrader's automatic minperiod machinery delay next() until enough bars exist, satisfying the canonical warm-up default without manual bar-skipping.

assumptions.choice: Exit conditions use momentum alone with no SMA check, while entry conditions require both momentum AND the SMA condition.
assumptions.reason: Spec states entries require momentum AND SMA, but exits are written as 'momentum < -5 (opposite signal)' / 'momentum > +5' with no SMA condition mentioned — implemented literally as written.
